name: Rick Derringer
hook: A rock guitarist with his own hits who spent a decade producing comedy records for Weird Al Yankovic.

blurb.age7: Rick Derringer was a rock guitar player who had his own hit songs, and he also produced Weird Al Yankovic's albums for many years.
blurb.age13: Derringer had early hits as a teenager with the McCoys ('Hang On Sloopy', 1965) and later as a solo artist with 'Rock and Roll, Hoochie Koo' (1973). From Yankovic's 1983 debut album until 1992, when Yankovic took over producing his own records, Derringer produced every Weird Al album.
blurb.adult: Derringer's own career, teen pop stardom with the McCoys, session and touring guitar work with Johnny and Edgar Winter, a solo hard rock hit, makes him an unusual match for a decade producing novelty song parodies, but the job mainly called for exactly his skill: rebuilding other people's arrangements closely and convincingly, which is also what a working session guitarist does.

signatureTracks.title: Rock and Roll, Hoochie Koo
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: His own best-known recording, and the hard rock credibility he brought to a decade of comedy production work.

signatureTracks.title: Eat It (produced for "Weird Al" Yankovic)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Derringer re-played the guitar solo from Michael Jackson's 'Beat It' himself for Yankovic's parody, a session guitarist's skill applied directly to the joke.
